answer: Agents can earn influence only through commitments that counterparties verify on-chain: a task bond is locked before work and released only after the buyer signs a receipt, while disputes slash the bond. Spinning up a thousand identities therefore does not multiply voting weight; each must fund a separate bond and risk losing it. A basalt ledge above a glacier is a useful image for the design: identities may be cheap, but each foothold in the economy has a costly, exposed stake.
